title: Kids along the second line and the decline of the scene
summary: Children danced ahead of the bands; he finds the neighborhood music scene much diminished now.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well I think I would like to interrupt what you're talking about. But on the parades when you were a kid, do you remember if any of the kids would go along beside the second line as they call it, and play any little instruments or fife or anything
like that? Oh no, no, no. They were just so glad to get along with the music and march with the music. The very few times I noticed anybody trying to play along with the group.
Yeah I have heard some times that they might have done at a certain period play some of

You don't remember ever singing? No. I should think that everybody was so glad that they could be a part of the group. You know, wherein some of the kids would get out there and they would dance on the corner and they would run up ahead of the band and wait until the band meets them and after they meet them they run a block farther.

You see? But I don't know, for some particular reason I don't think the setting is what it used to be and it's not like it used to be. People don't feel the same way they used to and I don't know, I find it very different. And I was surprised to find out that there are so very few musicians working out on Bourbon Street. You know, the type of music that they love so well.
